applicationPortal.value: Step 1: submit the ASU Graduate Admission application; for Performance: Keyboard (Organ, Piano Solo), select Music Performance (MM). Step 2: submit the separate School of Music, Dance and Theatre music application through the Music Application Portal after ASU login information is available. The music application requires three reference contacts, a resume PDF, program-specific materials, proof of English proficiency for non-native English speakers, and optional recorded audition upload where permitted. Piano MM applicants must upload a repertoire list divided into works studied and works publicly performed.

applicationFee.value: ASU Graduate Admission application fee: $70 for U.S. citizen, U.S. permanent resident, applicant in permanent-residency process, DACA, or international online student studying outside the U.S.; $115 for international students on any nonimmigrant visa type studying in the U.S. School of Music, Dance and Theatre fees: music application $10; prescreening $15 when applicable; recorded audition $65; late application $40.

auditionRequirements.value: Piano Solo MM audition dates: November 15, 2025 on campus for spring admission only; January 24, 2026 on campus; February 7, 2026 on campus; February 21, 2026 on campus and reserved for out-of-state applicants; recorded audition due February 1, 2026 and requires attendance at Virtual Experience Day on February 14, 2026. The recorded audition option is only available to master's applicants; in-person audition is highly recommended for scholarship and teaching-assistantship consideration. Recorded audition applicants join a large group meeting with keyboard faculty on February 14, 2026 and do not need to play piano on the virtual day. Recorded auditions are submitted in the music application through YouTube or Vimeo links and must follow ASU recording/submission guidelines. Applicants interested in a class-piano teaching assistantship must select Yes in the music application and upload a piano teaching demonstration in English with two complete lessons, preferably students at different levels; recommendation letters should address teaching ability.

repertoireRequirements.value: Final audition repertoire: Solo recital program of a minimum of 45 minutes. Final audition repertoire: Three complete works representing a variety of styles are required. Final audition repertoire: Concertos are not accepted. Final audition repertoire: Memorization is required except for complex contemporary works. Final audition repertoire: Movements or sections of larger works are not acceptable. Final audition repertoire: Be prepared to answer questions related to the musical and historical background of your audition repertoire. Final audition repertoire: No interior piano performance allowed. Final audition repertoire: ASU keyboard faculty encourage applicants to perform music by women, BIPOC, and under-represented composers.

Application deadline: Fall 2026 Performance: Conducting, Instrumental, Keyboard, Voice, Music Theatre and Opera deadline is December 1, 2025. Application deadline: ASU asks applicants to submit the Graduate Application, Music Application, and Proof of English Proficiency by the program application deadline. Recorded audition deadline: Spring 2026 recorded auditions for performance, pedagogy, and therapy applicants are due November 1, 2025, but the fully submitted music application is still due by the program deadline. Recorded audition deadline: Fall 2026 recorded auditions for performance, pedagogy, and therapy applicants are due February 1, 2026, but the fully submitted music application is still due by December 1, 2025. Audition dates: Piano Solo on-campus dates are November 15, 2025 for spring admission only, January 24, 2026, February 7, 2026, and February 21, 2026 for out-of-state applicants. Decision deadline: April 15 is the national deadline for graduate admission decisions when an offer is made.

englishScores.value: Minimum scores: TOEFL iBT taken in a testing center before January 21, 2026: 80; TOEFL iBT or TOEFL iBT Home Edition for exams taken on or after January 21, 2026: 4; IELTS Academic, IELTS Online, IELTS UKVI, or IELTS Indicator: 6.5 overall academic band; PTE: 60; Duolingo English Test: 105. Timing: The ASU music program requires proof of English proficiency before the program application deadline, and the School of Music, Dance and Theatre does not offer conditional admission. Test scores must be sent directly from the testing institution to ASU Graduate Admission Services. Validity: IELTS, PTE, TOEFL, or Duolingo exams must be taken no more than two years before the student's ASU start date. Exemptions: Automatic exemptions apply to U.S. citizens, U.S. permanent residents, and citizens of countries or territories on ASU's English-speaking country and territory list; other exemption routes require a form after applying, such as qualifying English-medium degree, U.S. degree, approved-country degree, eligible graduate coursework, eligible U.S. undergraduate coursework, or four years of U.S. high school education. Notes: ASU does not accept TOEFL iBT Paper Edition, accepts only electronic TOEFL score reports, ASU institutional code is 4007, and ASU does not accept PTE Academic Online. Program note: some programs may have higher requirements or may not accept certain tests, so the music deadline and program page remain the source of record for timing.

auditionRequirements.value: Collaborative Piano MM audition dates: November 15, 2025 on campus for spring admission only; January 31, 2026 on campus; February 14, 2026 on campus. Applicants may bring their own collaborative partner or use one provided by ASU; if using ASU partners, repertoire substitutions are not allowed. Exact rehearsal and audition times are sent one week before the audition day. Tests in sight-reading and foreign languages are given. Applicants are asked about prior language study and assessed on pronunciation in French, German, and Italian. ASU's graduate music application page lists the MM Piano Solo/Collaborative audition as live and in-person or uploaded recorded audition, but the Collaborative Piano audition page lists on-campus dates and partner logistics as the specific MM Collaborative Piano instructions.

Final audition repertoire: One of the following instrumental works: Schumann, Fantasiestucke, Op. 73; Brahms, Sonata in f minor, Op. 120, #1, Movement I; Brahms, Sonata in E-flat major, Op. 120, #2, Movement I. Final audition repertoire: Three solo compositions from contrasting stylistic periods performed from memory; individual movements from larger works are allowed. Final audition repertoire: ASU keyboard faculty encourage applicants to perform music by women, BIPOC, and under-represented composers.

applicationPortal.value: Apply through Ball State Graduate Admissions for Music (MM) - Performance. The program page states that materials are uploaded in the Cardinal Landing Portal, including the School of Music supplemental form, interview scheduling/contact step, letter of intent, three recommendation letters, current resume or curriculum vitae, and audition/portfolio materials. Performance applicants may schedule an in-person audition in the portal on a main audition day, arrange an alternate date when needed, or upload a recorded audition as the portfolio.

applicationFee.value: Graduate applications are $60 per program and the fee is nonrefundable. Ball State lists fee waivers for currently enrolled Ball State students or alumni, eligible current employees, veterans or active-duty military, guest students seeking transfer credits, and prospective students who attended a Ball State graduate program information session.

sources.label: Ball State Music MM Performance Application

auditionRequirements.value: Performance applicants must complete an audition for admission to the School of Music. For piano degree programs, Ball State strongly encourages a live audition but accepts recorded auditions. For on-campus auditions, applicants submit the completed School of Music application, including preferred audition date, by January 1. Video audition applicants select Recorded Audition in the application; faculty may follow up with a video interview. Applicants unable to attend published audition days may email musicaudition@bsu.edu about an ad hoc audition. For full graduate assistantship consideration, Ball State advises submitting the application and completing the audition by March 1.

repertoireRequirements.value: Final audition repertoire: Master of Music in Piano Performance requires a solo program of approximately 50 minutes in length with at least three contrasting styles represented. Final audition repertoire: Sight-reading is required. Final audition repertoire: Ball State strongly encourages a live audition for piano degree programs but accepts recorded auditions.

deadlines.value: Program application deadline for Music (MM) - Performance: February 1 to start in Fall; December 1 to start in Spring; for Summer, the application must be completed two weeks before the semester begins. On-campus School of Music audition scheduling deadline: January 1 for the completed School of Music application with preferred audition date. Listed on-campus audition dates: February 7, February 15, February 20, and February 21. Graduate assistantship full-consideration advisory date: submit the application and complete the audition by March 1. International applicants must submit all materials by the earliest applicable deadline, either the international deadline or the program deadline; Ball State lists international application deadlines as June 15 for Fall, November 15 for Spring, and March 15 for Summer.

englishScores.value: Ball State requires applicants with an education history outside the U.S. to submit English proficiency unless they qualify for a waiver. Official scores must be sent electronically to Ball State Admissions; school code 1051 and admissions@bsu.edu are listed. Scores are valid for 24 months. Required English proficiency scores include TOEFL 79, IELTS Academic 6.5, Duolingo 110, Pearson PTE 53, SAT Critical Reading or Evidence-Based Reading and Writing 500, or ACT English 21. Ball State accepts TOEFL iBT MyBest scores. The Academic Bridge Program may be available at slightly lower scores: Duolingo 100 or 105, TOEFL 75-78, IELTS Academic 6.0, or Pearson PTE 51-52. Ball State notes that academic programs or departments may have different English proficiency requirements.

Boston Conservatory Graduate Music Audition Requirements

applicationPortal.value: Step 1: submit the Boston Conservatory at Berklee online application. Step 2: after submitting the online application, complete the required music pre-screen through SlideRoom; instructions are emailed after application submission. Step 3: submit supporting materials, including official transcripts, English proficiency material if required, and music recommendation material. Music applicants need at least one recommendation letter, and recommender information is entered in the supplemental application through SlideRoom. Admission requires both academic and artistic acceptance.

auditionRequirements.value: Prescreening: Piano requires a pre-screen; all piano applicants must submit a pre-screen video recording by the application deadline before they can be considered for a live audition. Scheduling: after the application is submitted, applicants receive instructions to register for an audition in the application portal under My Events; if the major requires a pre-screen, the pre-screen must be submitted by the deadline first. Audition format: Boston Conservatory strongly encourages in-person auditions when possible, but offers regional and online alternatives as permitted; online auditions are held live on Zoom and use the same audition requirements as in-person auditions. 2026 Piano audition dates: January 18, 2026 on campus; February 8, 2026 on campus; February 15, 2026 on campus; February 21, 2026 on campus.

sources.label: Boston Conservatory Audition Dates and Locations
Boston Conservatory Graduate Music Audition Requirements

repertoireRequirements.value: Prescreening repertoire: Minimum 30-minute pre-screen video recording. Prescreening repertoire: Must include the virtuosic etude and at least three additional pieces chosen from the audition requirements. Prescreening repertoire: A movement or movements from the classical sonata or from multi-movement Romantic or contemporary pieces may be used if the total pre-screen program is at least 30 minutes. Final audition repertoire: Prepare every required category. Final audition repertoire: A prelude and fugue from The Well-Tempered Clavier, or another Bach work that includes a fugue. Final audition repertoire: A complete sonata by Haydn, Mozart, Beethoven, or Schubert. Final audition repertoire: A major solo piano work from the Romantic era, including Rachmaninoff. Final audition repertoire: A solo piano piece from the 20th or 21st century. Final audition repertoire: One virtuosic etude, such as Chopin, Liszt, Debussy, Rachmaninoff, Scriabin, or Ligeti. Final audition repertoire: Multi-movement works must be prepared in their entirety. Final audition repertoire: All works must be performed from memory. Final audition repertoire: Incomplete audition requirements will not be accepted. Additional repertoire notes: Applicants are encouraged to program creatively and show something unique about themselves as musicians.

sources.label: Boston Conservatory Graduate Music Audition Requirements

deadlines.value: Application opens: July 1. Recommended pre-screen deadline for Regular Action: November 1. Regular Action application and required pre-screen materials deadline: December 1. englishScores.value: Minimum scores: Master of Music in Performance, Composition, or Conducting: TOEFL iBT exams taken before January 21, 2026: 79; TOEFL iBT exams taken on or after January 21, 2026: 4; IELTS overall band guideline: 6.5; Duolingo English Test: 115. Come scoglio; Der Schauspieldirektor, Bester Jüngling. auditionRequirements.value: Prescreening: all programs require a prescreening video recording or portfolio due at the online application deadline of December 1. Video quality: professional production is not required, but sound quality should accurately represent the performance; lighting should be adequate and the camera should show full range of movement and use of instrument. Piano-specific recorded audition note: applicants who already submitted recordings of a complete program for prescreening are not required to submit additional audition recordings. Final recorded auditions: all recordings must be recent and recorded no earlier than the previous June. Video auditions are due February 1 for approved applicants and are only allowed for applicants to certain programs who live outside a 500-mile radius of NEC.

repertoireRequirements.value: Prescreening repertoire: A complete Classical sonata, for example music by Beethoven, Haydn, Mozart, Schubert, or others. Final audition repertoire: Applicants must prepare four vocal pieces chosen from Strauss: Allerseelen; Barber: The Monk and His Cat; Brahms: Meine Liebe ist Grün; Schubert: Ganymed; Debussy: C'est l'extase; Puccini: Mi chiamano Mimi. auditionRequirements.value: A prescreening video is required for all MM/MME applicants. Collaborative Piano applicants are notified if they advance to the audition round to perform on campus. repertoireRequirements.value: Prescreening repertoire: The first or last movement of a major instrumental duo sonata, such as Mozart K. 301 or later, Beethoven, Brahms, Chopin, Faure, or similar. Prescreening repertoire: This instrumental duo sonata selection may be the same selection from the live audition requirements. Prescreening repertoire: Two contrasting art songs, lieder, or melodie in different styles and languages; these may be the same selections used for the live audition. Prescreening repertoire: A seven-to-ten-minute solo piano work of the applicant's choice played from memory. Final audition repertoire: Applicants are encouraged to bring their own collaborative partners for the live audition; TCU can provide partners upon request if requested in the online application as early as possible in the audition season. Final audition repertoire: Choose one piece from Group A: Mozart Sonata for Piano and Violin in E-flat major, K. 380, 1st movement; Beethoven Sonata for Piano and Violin No. 7 in C minor, Op. 30, no. 2, 1st movement; or Brahms Sonata for Piano and Violin No. 1 in G major, Op. 78, 1st movement. Final audition repertoire: Choose one piece from Group B: Schumann Cello Concerto in A minor, Op. 129, 1st movement, beginning to downbeat of measure 96 with no cuts; Dvorak Cello Concerto in B minor, Op. 104, 1st movement, 12 measures before the cello's first entrance to Rehearsal no. 9; or Elgar Cello Concerto in E minor, Op. 85, 4th movement, Rehearsal 65 to end. Final audition repertoire: Faculty will select one of the following songs at the audition, in original keys: Schubert, Gretchen am Spinnrade; Barber, St. Ita's Vision; or Debussy, Green. Final audition repertoire: A seven-to-ten-minute solo piano piece of the applicant's choice, played from memory; it may be the same as the prescreening solo piece. Final audition repertoire: Sight-reading. Additional repertoire notes: For specific audition repertoire questions, TCU directs applicants to Michael Bukhman, Associate Professor.

auditionRequirements.value: MM Piano auditions are offered in person and video-recorded formats; In-person auditions are preferred, but recorded auditions receive equal consideration; Pre-screening materials are due December 1; The pre-screening video must show the applicant's hands and profile at all times; Video-recorded audition submissions are due Thursday, February 12, 2026; Applicants who choose the February 12 recorded audition deadline will not have the option to switch to an in-person audition; Recorded audition applicants must submit a speaking video answering these prompts: state your name and degree(s), describe your goals for graduate study as a graduate pianist and your career, and describe what kinds of repertoire you are interested in pursuing in your next degree; YouTube links are not accepted; Original files or downloadable links from file-hosting platforms are acceptable, with Google Drive preferred.

repertoireRequirements.value: MM Piano Performance requirements: Pre-screening repertoire must be at least three contrasting pieces; Pre-screening repertoire may include movements of larger works; Final audition repertoire must include a major work of J. S. Bach, such as a prelude and fugue from the Well-Tempered Clavier, a suite, or a partita; Final audition repertoire must include a complete Classical sonata, for example one by Mozart, Haydn, Beethoven, or Schubert; Final audition repertoire must include a work of the applicant's choice from the 19th, 20th, or 21st centuries, excluding works considered Classical as in the sonata requirement; Final audition repertoire must include an etude of virtuosity; All works listed in the final audition requirements must be performed from memory and in their entirety for video-recorded auditions; Memorization is required; Audition repertoire may duplicate pre-screening repertoire; Applicants must submit a complete alphabetized repertoire list of all major works studied from Bach Inventions and higher in difficulty.

deadlines.value: Most graduate degree application materials are due December 1. MM Piano prescreening video is due December 1. Recorded auditions for invited Fall 2026 MM Piano applicants are due February 12, 2026.

englishScores.value: For master's applicants: TOEFL iBT 88, IELTS 6.5, ECPE 650, or MET 56. Scores must be submitted by the application deadline; SMTD does not accept Duolingo.

applicationFee.value: MM / Specialist Artistic Profile fee: $120. Late fee: $25. Fees are non-refundable.

applicationPortal.value: MM applicants submit the SMTD Artistic Profile. UMich SMTD lists MM in Collaborative Piano as a graduate degree in the Department of Piano.

auditionRequirements.value: MM Collaborative Piano auditions are offered in person and online; in-person auditions are preferred but online auditions receive equal consideration. Applicants who advance meet faculty for live playing, sight-reading, brief German/Italian/French diction exams, and an interview.

repertoireRequirements.value: MM Collaborative Piano prescreening: unedited videos totaling 30 minutes of works for voice/instrument(s) and piano, with 15 minutes for voice and piano and 15 minutes for instrument(s) and piano, plus recommended recent collaborative videos, repertoire lists, proposed audition program, and speaking video. Audition repertoire includes one listed sonata movement, four listed art songs, one listed song by a specified composer, and one solo piece under 10 minutes; memorization is not required.

deadlines.value: Most graduate degree application materials are due December 1. Collaborative Piano prescreening materials are uploaded to the SMTD Artistic Profile by the application deadline.

englishScores.value: For master's applicants: TOEFL iBT 88, IELTS 6.5, ECPE 650, or MET 56. Scores must be submitted by the application deadline; SMTD does not accept Duolingo.

applicationPortal.value: Apply through the University of Minnesota graduate application for the School of Music; upload required program-specific materials and audition videos in the Digital Uploads section when required.

applicationFee.value: School of Music applicants pay a $50 School of Music fee in addition to the Graduate School application fee; exact current Graduate School fee should be verified on the Graduate School fee page before submission.

auditionRequirements.value: The School of Music strongly encourages in-person auditions on scheduled dates, but accepts prerecorded auditions in most performance areas; video submissions must be recorded within the past 12 months, with each selection performed from beginning to end in one take and no editing within individual selections; complete in-person auditions and complete video auditions are accepted for piano based on prescreening results.

repertoireRequirements.value: Prescreening: Submit a prescreening video with the application for MM Piano Performance; the prescreen must include the first movement of a Classical sonata by Beethoven, Haydn, Mozart, or Clementi, and one other work by a different composer from the 19th, 20th, or 21st century; Final audition repertoire: Prepare all audition repertoire from memory; Bach prelude and fugue from The Well-Tempered Clavier or several substantial movements from a Bach suite or partita; a complete major sonata by Haydn, Mozart, or Beethoven; a representative work from the 19th century; a representative work from the 20th century; at least one of the 19th- or 20th-century works should be technically and interpretively demanding and at least 10 minutes long.

deadlines.value: December 1, 2025: School of Music graduate application deadline; January 24, 2026 and February 7, 2026: listed instrumental-performance audition dates; audition videos are submitted by the application deadline through Digital Uploads.

englishScores.value: English minimums include TOEFL iBT 79 total with writing 21 and reading 19 for tests before January 21, 2026; TOEFL iBT 4.5 total, writing 4.5, and reading 4.5 for tests on or after January 21, 2026; IELTS Academic 6.5 total with writing 6.5 and reading 6.5; Duolingo 115 overall with writing 115 and reading 115; PTE Academic 59 total with writing 59 and reading 59; scores must generally be within two years, and MyBest is not accepted for the minimum total.

applicationPortal.value: Apply through the University of Minnesota graduate application for the School of Music; upload required program-specific materials and audition videos in the Digital Uploads section when required.

applicationFee.value: School of Music applicants pay a $50 School of Music fee in addition to the Graduate School application fee; exact current Graduate School fee should be verified on the Graduate School fee page before submission.

auditionRequirements.value: Collaborative Piano and Coaching requires a prescreen video and in-person auditions; applicants who pass screening are invited to a live campus audition; partners and rehearsal times are assigned as part of the live audition process; a personal interview may be conducted by faculty.

repertoireRequirements.value: Prescreening: For both MM and DMA, record two contrasting collaborative piano works with partners; prescreening performances are not necessarily restricted to the audition repertoire; Final audition repertoire: Mozart Sonata for Piano and Violin in E minor K. 304, either movement; Brahms Von ewiger Liebe in the original key; Libby Larsen Lift Me Into Heaven Slowly in the original key; sight-reading from instrumental and/or vocal repertoire.

deadlines.value: December 1, 2025: School of Music graduate application deadline; January 24, 2026 and February 7, 2026: listed instrumental-performance audition dates; audition videos are submitted by the application deadline through Digital Uploads.

applicationPortal.value: Apply through the UNCG Graduate School application for the School of Music; required materials include transcripts, two recommendations, personal statement, and any area-specific audition or interview materials.

applicationFee.value: Graduate application fee is $65; current UNCG students may be eligible for waiver according to the School of Music graduate application page.

auditionRequirements.value: After faculty review of the application, selected performance applicants are invited for a live audition and interview; international students outside the United States may select Other as audition date and faculty determine whether a virtual interview will be scheduled.

repertoireRequirements.value: Final audition repertoire: Piano Performance applicants should prepare approximately 25 minutes of repertoire representing three contrasting style periods, preferably from memory; applicants are encouraged to include a work composed after 1950; applicants are also encouraged to include a work by a composer whose background reflects a different racial, gender, gender-identity, sexual-identity, or cultural tradition than the standard repertoire.

deadlines.value: January 15: assistantship-consideration deadline for MM Performance All Others; July 1: application deadline for MM Performance All Others; 2025-2026 audition dates include January 17, February 14, and February 28, 2026; February 28 is listed as priority music-scholarship audition date.

englishScores.value: UNCG international requirements list proof of English proficiency for non-native English speakers; applicants should verify the current Graduate School test table for accepted TOEFL, IELTS, Duolingo, or waiver options because the admissions page houses the official score details.

applicationPortal.value: Apply through the UNCG Graduate School application for the School of Music; required materials include transcripts, two recommendations, personal statement, and collaborative-piano audition/interview materials.

applicationFee.value: Graduate application fee is $65; current UNCG students may be eligible for waiver according to the School of Music graduate application page.

auditionRequirements.value: Collaborative Piano auditions are conducted by recorded performance, with live or in-person auditions possible by request to Dr. James Douglass; each audition includes an interview through Microsoft Teams on the posted audition date or in person; campus visits are optional; applicants will sight-read during the interview.

repertoireRequirements.value: Prescreening: Video materials should include four to five vocal art songs representing a variety of styles, composers, and historical periods, with poetic and word-for-word translations; Prescreening: Include a 15-minute program of instrumental works representing a variety of styles, composers, and historical periods; Prescreening: Choose either a solo work of approximately five minutes, preferably from memory, or an additional five minutes of instrumental works for a 20-minute instrumental total; Prescreening: Applicants are encouraged to include a work by a composer whose background reflects a different racial, gender, gender-identity, sexual-identity, or cultural tradition than the standard repertoire; Final audition repertoire: Official audition phase uses a 25 to 30 minute recital program with representative instrumental and vocal repertoire that does not duplicate the prescreen works; repertoire should represent a variety of styles, composers, and historical periods; sight-reading occurs during the live interview; applicants should contact Dr. Douglass to confirm repertoire.

deadlines.value: January 15: assistantship-consideration deadline for MM Performance All Others; July 1: application deadline for MM Performance All Others; 2025-2026 audition dates include January 17, February 14, and February 28, 2026; February 28 is listed as priority music-scholarship audition date.

englishScores.value: UNCG international requirements list proof of English proficiency for non-native English speakers; applicants should verify the current Graduate School test table for accepted TOEFL, IELTS, Duolingo, or waiver options because the admissions page houses the official score details.

applicationPortal.value: Apply to UNT Graduate Admissions through GradCAS first; after receiving the UNT Student ID, complete the College of Music application through Acceptd, which opens September 1 each year and serves as the application for audition, admission, and music merit awards.

applicationFee.value: The College of Music application fee is $40; the UNT Graduate Admissions GradCAS application has a separate fee that is charged in GradCAS at submission.

auditionRequirements.value: All graduate areas require screening; screening is a preliminary audition round consisting of audition videos submitted through Acceptd; all screening and final audition videos must include both audio and video, be unedited, have no artificial audio enhancement, and be recorded within the past six months; final audition videos must include all required audition materials; some areas may require a live virtual component; for Piano, all graduate applicants submit a video screening recording to determine advancement; the screening repertoire is the same as the live audition repertoire; both on-campus and off-campus auditions are scheduled in January and February; a live audition is recommended for entering graduate performance students; all movements of a multi-movement work should be submitted in one continuous take; proof of UNT English Language Proficiency is required before an MM or DMA piano applicant can be scheduled for an audition or have a final video audition reviewed, and no admission or music award offer can be made until English proficiency is demonstrated.

repertoireRequirements.value: Prescreening: All graduate piano applicants are required to submit a video screening recording; the repertoire for the screening is the same as the live audition repertoire; all movements of a multi-movement work should be submitted in one continuous take; Final audition repertoire: Master's Level comprises a fifteen-minute program from memory; Final audition repertoire: A Prelude and Fugue of J. S. Bach or a complete Toccata, Suite, or Partita from which the faculty will choose a few movements; Final audition repertoire: A complete Classical-era sonata; Final audition repertoire: A work from the Romantic, Impressionistic, or Contemporary periods.

deadlines.value: September 1: College of Music application opens each year; November 1: Spring 2026 application deadline if the area accepts spring applications; November 1: Fall 2026 deadline for consideration for live audition/interview on the December audition date; December 1: preference deadline for January or February audition dates; February 1: final deadline to submit music application and video auditions for Piano applicants; mid-March: admission results notification; April 15: deadline to accept or decline admission offer.

englishScores.value: All international applicants must show proof of English language proficiency. Accepted English proficiency exam minimums include TOEFL iBT 79 for exams taken before January 21, 2026, or TOEFL iBT 4 for exams taken on or after January 21, 2026; IELTS Academic 6.0 overall band; PTE 53; Duolingo English Test 100; Michigan English Test four-skill exam section scores of 54; or Cambridge C1 Advanced/C2 Proficiency at C1. TOEFL MyBest is excluded; ETS school code is 6481; tests must generally be taken within two years prior to applying. UNT also accepts listed exemption pathways, including citizenship or qualifying education in an approved English-speaking country, qualifying academic English coursework, and completion of UNT IELI Level 6.

applicationPortal.value: Apply to UNT Graduate Admissions through GradCAS first; after receiving the UNT Student ID, complete the College of Music application through Acceptd and select the collaborative piano program/area as instructed.

applicationFee.value: The College of Music application fee is $40; the UNT Graduate Admissions GradCAS application has a separate fee that is charged in GradCAS at submission.

auditionRequirements.value: Collaborative Piano applicants submit a completed online application including a comprehensive repertoire list for all genres; the audition will not be scheduled until all materials are received; screening recordings must state the applicant's name and degree sought at the beginning or embed that information in the video; recordings should be unedited, reflect one take as in live performance, and be no more than one year old; screening recordings are due on or before December 1 and are reviewed by collaborative piano faculty; applicants applying for live audition are notified before the end of December; UNT provides partners for all in-person auditions; live audition is strongly recommended; final audition by recording is allowed, but UNT cannot provide partners for recorded auditions and candidates auditioning by recording may be requested to interview via Zoom.

repertoireRequirements.value: Prescreening: Master's Level screening materials include 15-30 minutes of instrumental duo repertoire; Prescreening: 10-20 minutes of vocal repertoire representing several styles and languages; Prescreening: One solo work, memorized, 5-10 minutes in length; Prescreening: A video introducing yourself and discussing collaborative experience and professional goals; Prescreening: Optional videos of coaching, conducting, or teaching are welcome, and additional performance recordings may be submitted as supplementary material; Final audition repertoire: Beethoven Cello Sonata Op. 69 in A major, first movement, until recapitulation; Final audition repertoire: Strauss Allerseelen in E-flat; Final audition repertoire: Faure Mandoline in A-flat; Final audition repertoire: Sing and play Barber The Daisies in any key and any octave; Final audition repertoire: One solo work, memorized, 5-10 minutes in length; Final audition repertoire: Sightreading; Final audition repertoire: Discussion of past work and future goals.

deadlines.value: September 1: College of Music application opens each year; November 1: Spring 2026 application deadline if the area accepts spring applications; November 1: Fall 2026 deadline for consideration for live audition/interview on the December audition date; December 1: Collaborative Piano screening recordings due and preference deadline for January or February audition dates; February 15: final deadline for most areas and recorded final collaborative-piano audition materials if auditioning by recording; mid-March: admission results notification; April 15: deadline to accept or decline admission offer.

englishScores.value: All international applicants must show proof of English language proficiency. Accepted English proficiency exam minimums include TOEFL iBT 79 for exams taken before January 21, 2026, or TOEFL iBT 4 for exams taken on or after January 21, 2026; IELTS Academic 6.0 overall band; PTE 53; Duolingo English Test 100; Michigan English Test four-skill exam section scores of 54; or Cambridge C1 Advanced/C2 Proficiency at C1. TOEFL MyBest is excluded; ETS school code is 6481; tests must generally be taken within two years prior to applying. UNT also accepts listed exemption pathways, including citizenship or qualifying education in an approved English-speaking country, qualifying academic English coursework, and completion of UNT IELI Level 6.

auditionRequirements.value: Piano MM requires prescreening videos in the Butler School application by December 1; Individual movements or excerpts should be uploaded as separate digital files; Video format is required and audio-only submissions are not accepted; Recordings must be genuinely performed by the applicant, unedited, and without reverb/effects; Prescreening results are released in mid-December; Auditions take place at the Butler School; Applicants outside the continental United States may audition by video, due with the music application by the application deadline; If invited, live audition duration is shorter than the prepared 45 minutes; Applicants who submit the optional teaching assistantship video will have a 10-15 minute interview with the piano pedagogy professor.

repertoireRequirements.value: Prescreening requirements: The prescreening recording must include a solo recital-style program of at least 45 minutes of music; Prescreening requirements: Applicants should select pieces representing the highest level of musicality and ability; Prescreening requirements: A minimum of three styles should be represented; Prescreening requirements: The program must include all or part of a major work from the Classical period; Prescreening requirements: Concertos and other non-solo works are not preferred or recommended; Prescreening requirements: Optional teaching assistantship applicants must request an interview and submit a 10-20 minute unedited sample teaching video showing interaction with students in private instruction or classroom piano; Final audition repertoire: If invited, 45 minutes of music should be prepared; Final audition repertoire: Live audition duration will be shorter than 45 minutes.

deadlines.value: September 1: Butler School application opens; December 1: University of Texas application due; December 1: Butler School application due; December 1: Prescreening videos due; December 11: Transcripts, test scores, and recommendation letters due; Mid-December: Prescreen results and live audition invitations; January 15: FAFSA priority deadline; January 24, January 25, February 7, and February 8, 2026: Piano live audition dates; On or before March 1: Admission decisions; On or before April 1: Butler merit-based scholarship notifications; April 15: Response deadline.
